sample_campaign_canonical_content: Position OpenPost as the publishing workspace between AI agents and social accounts. Show one source brief becoming distinct destination renditions, human review before scheduling, provider credentials staying inside OpenPost, and one visible queue. Keep every platform's version native. Call to action: openpost.social.
sample_campaign_handoff_read_body: An agent can use read-only OpenPost operations to inspect workspace content and provider capabilities without receiving provider credentials.

sample_campaign_complete_body: In a real campaign, the next step is an explicit schedule or publish action against connected accounts.
sample_campaign_local_only: This sample makes no campaign or provider calls. It does not create accounts, expose provider credentials, save drafts, use your publishing quota, or add anything to the queue. On the managed app, account connection, media upload, scheduling, and publishing require an active or trial plan.
sample_campaign_x_content:
An AI agent prepared this launch for five networks without receiving any provider credentials.

I reviewed each version in OpenPost, then moved the campaign toward one visible queue.

Open source. Hosted or self-hosted.
openpost.social
sample_campaign_linkedin_content:
AI can write a launch post. It should not publish one blind.

For this campaign, an agent prepared one base draft and five destination-specific versions in OpenPost. It never received our provider credentials. I reviewed the copy and suggested schedule before anything could move to the publishing queue.

OpenPost is the open-source publishing workspace between agents and social accounts — hosted or self-hosted.
sample_campaign_bluesky_content:
AI can help prepare a launch without holding the keys to every social account.

This version was tailored for Bluesky, reviewed in OpenPost, and kept out of the queue until a human approves the schedule.

Open source: openpost.social
sample_campaign_mastodon_content:
Today we're showing a practical agent workflow: inspect publishing context, prepare a canonical draft, adapt it for each destination, then hand every version back for human review.

The agent works through OpenPost. Provider credentials stay inside OpenPost, and the queue stays visible.

Hosted or self-hosted: openpost.social
sample_campaign_threads_content:
One launch brief. Five versions that do not read like copies of each other.

An agent prepared the campaign in OpenPost without receiving provider credentials. A human reviewed every destination before scheduling.

That control is the product.

Your MCP client controls the approval prompt, so authorize only a client you trust and prefer the current-workspace boundary. Saved provider credentials are never returned to the client.
